body:
Router now defaults routed geolocation headers to removal and requires explicit per-request consent before forwarding supported location metadata. It also hardens the existing client privacy defaults and documents the limits of those controls. This draft remains unfinished: universal tool/account privacy and the complete JavaScript-first parity requirements have not been verified.

Fixes #784

## Behavior and reproduction

Before this change, clients could forward geolocation and ingress network metadata without an explicit location-sharing request. The Router request path now parses and validates the consent control, strips it before upstream forwarding, rejects ambiguous values, and removes location and ingress network headers by default. The explicit location opt-in does not authorize forwarding ingress identity headers. Provider-specific, retry, streaming, management, and persisted-policy routes retain regression coverage. Client configuration and documentation distinguish routed request controls from direct vendor traffic, account settings, source-IP visibility, OAuth, MCP, telemetry and retention.

This does not establish a universal vendor/account geolocation guarantee. The remaining acceptance inventory and investigation are in [the case study](docs/case-studies/issue-784/README.md). No required sub-issues were identified. No existing feature was intentionally removed.

## Current coordinated repair batch

The previous published head is `4ea091242db0a51a07415c8c04a23a6db0b8c04b`, tested merge `d584507d683d08b53d74f109d6f5f0ebeddb2b72`. [Run 42863382776](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/42863382776) completed at 2026-11-10 18:39:47 UTC. All 59 jobs and all three applicable workflows are terminal; all 24 nonpassing logs and all 26 complete artifacts were collected and inspected before this push. No CI run was cancelled. The [terminal review](docs/case-studies/issue-784/ci-4ea-terminal-20261110.md) records every failure and whole-byte custody, with negative controls classified separately.

The coordinated batch through `93995ee40be4b570becbe0b788dba58f5bd0ea6f`:

- Repairs selected Git census source-history assertions by composing the exact original/current controller sources, complete inverses and fresh batched CST/native binding checks. All five original cases pass in Node and Bun within unchanged deadlines.
- Runs actual reverse regeneration and reviews all three changed artifacts. The complete twelve-case original Node translator file and independent deadline audit pass. Its changed module still has 701 unsupported items and zero translated items; no executable gain is claimed.
- Retains the complete negative runtime-scope performance comparison; no production optimization or speed gain is claimed.
- Preserves all terminal CI artifacts and both current complete local-gate attempts. Only identified inactive duplicate task files are retired after full original-byte verification, with reclaimed-space and custody receipts.

Earlier changes include the actual producer's 20 refreshed canonical outputs, complete Schemars/nullable/operation/Default source-history repairs and their whole-file regression evidence. The checked-in inventory has 162 executable top-level production functions out of 2578 and 2416 carried production functions; these counts do not establish full parity. The newest canonical CI ZIP remains unqualified data: it is retained whole but has not been installed or joined to subsequent local compiler changes.

## Validation and limitations

Installed TypeScript is **5.9.3**, Node is **20.20.2**, and local Bun is **1.4.4**; CI pins Bun 1.4.3. Original strictness, whole test files, original case/child/job deadlines and compiler size limits remain unchanged.

- Selected census receiving: five cases pass in each engine; the initial failed Node attempt is retained.
- Reverse freshness: actual generation changes exactly three artifacts; all twelve original Node translator cases and the full independent audit pass. The complete Bun attempt passes nine cases before the unchanged container memory guard interrupts regeneration; its default deadline and remaining file stay unqualified.
- Corrected complete local gate at `bcf84c063f06754ba48aa7d2c4c23e48bfdbd5ce`: all ten lint commands, both 259-case native runtime suites, ten deadline controls, public/native declarations, native freshness and strict 167-file TypeScript compilation pass.
- The whole nine-case native TypeScript file completes, including all compiled Node/Bun runtime expectations, but its original regeneration drift case takes **78857.500265/60000 ms**. The independent deadline audit fails correctly.
- The unchanged memory observer then interrupts parity acceptance after 104 completed assertions, at **2867023872 bytes** within the **3135369216-byte** container. Nine later TypeScript commands, strict parity and all forward/reverse checks are unrun for that attempt. Its exact full evidence and the separate invalid npm-PATH launch are in [the gate report](docs/case-studies/issue-784/current-complete-gates-20261110.md).

**Still required:** fresh same-SHA green CI and the complete local gate; complete independent semantic review and canonical regeneration; genuine complete owned/profile matrices and reverse-owned freshness; strict parity and every original test/child/job deadline; universal tool/account privacy acceptance. The terminal CI cycle still has 441 draft parity gaps, incomplete matrices, missing owned matrix TypeScript inputs, long-running original compiler cases and job cancellations. Failures also present on main remain mandatory. No missing secret or manual access was identified, so no credential-dependent skip or manual-action workaround was introduced. Rust remains blocked until every required JavaScript stage passes for the same SHA. No Rust tool runs locally.

Latest fetched main is `eb2dad1c0a18394dc1aad46413e11401e74eb502`, already an ancestor. The issue has no comments or required sub-issues; all seven PR conversation comments, zero inline comments and zero reviews were refreshed and read. The PR remains draft and unmerged. This feedback checkpoint establishes no completion or release readiness.
